claims.text: The solution-treated MoNbTaTi reference alloy has a homogeneous, disordered A2 matrix.
Aging solution-treated MoNbTaTi at approximately 750°C for 2 hours will form B2-type nanoprecipitates.
The aging-induced B2-type precipitates will be coherent with the A2 matrix.
The aging-induced precipitates will be uniformly distributed and smaller than 50 nm.
The nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase the alloy's yield strength.
The fine precipitate distribution will promote heterogeneous strain distribution.
Nano-twinning will be activated at precipitate–matrix interfaces.
At room temperature, the aged alloy will have significantly higher yield strength than the solution-treated non-aged alloy.
At room temperature, the aged alloy will maintain or improve plasticity relative to the solution-treated non-aged alloy.
Coarse, nonuniform, or incoherent precipitates could eliminate the anticipated strength–plasticity improvement.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says ductility will be enhanced, while the predicted outcome permits plasticity merely to be maintained. The falsification rule is stricter still, requiring a statistically significant improvement in both yield strength and ductility.

The boundary field conditions the hypothesis on successful formation of uniform coherent sub-50 nm precipitates, whereas the falsification rule treats failure to form those precipitates as falsification rather than as failure of the stated boundary condition.
